title: Pipeline Hazards
objective: Find the load-use hazard in a program on the 5-stage pipeline, compare it with a pipeline without forwarding, then reorder the code so it runs without any stall.
explanation:
The 5-stage processor overlaps instructions: while one instruction is in EX, the next one is already being decoded (ID) and the one after that fetched (IF). If an instruction needs a register that an older instruction has not written yet, there is a read-after-write (RAW) data dependency.

Ripes' 5-stage processor has a forwarding unit: results are passed from the EX/MEM and MEM/WB pipeline registers straight to the ALU inputs, so most dependencies cost nothing. A load only has its data after the MEM stage, so an instruction that uses the loaded register immediately must wait one cycle. The hazard detection unit then freezes IF and ID and inserts a bubble into EX: a stall.

CPI (cycles per instruction) = cycles / retired instructions. Every stall cycle increases it. The Explorer tab shows held instructions and bubbles in the timeline; all numbers come from the recorded trace of the Ripes model.
example:
# Mission 2: find the load-use hazard
.data
values: .word 7, 5
.text
    la   t0, values
    lw   t1, 0(t0)      # load first value
    add  t2, t1, t1     # uses t1 immediately: load-use hazard
    lw   t3, 4(t0)      # load second value
    addi t4, x0, 1
    add  t5, t3, t4     # t3 was loaded two instructions earlier

steps.title: Load the program on the 5-stage processor
steps.instruction: Click Load example and Select processor (5-stage processor with forwarding and hazard detection).

steps.title: Find the stall
steps.instruction: Run the program. In the Explorer tab, look for the cycle where add t2, t1, t1 (disassembled as add x7 x6 x6) is held and a stall bubble enters EX. Click the instruction: its explanation names the load it depends on.

steps.title: Remove the forwarding unit
steps.instruction: Select the 5-stage processor without forwarding unit (RV32_5S_NO_FW) via the processor selection dialog and run the same program again. Every dependency on a recent result now has to wait for write-back. Compare the stall count and CPI.

challenge.text: Switch back to the 5-stage processor (RV32_5S). Reorder the instructions so that t2 = 14 and t5 = 6 still hold, but the program runs with zero stall cycles.
challenge.hint: Give the first load more time: move an independent instruction between lw t1 and its use.
challenge.reference_solution:
.data
values: .word 7, 5
.text
    la   t0, values
    lw   t1, 0(t0)
    lw   t3, 4(t0)
    add  t2, t1, t1
    addi t4, x0, 1
    add  t5, t3, t4

completion: You used the trace to locate a load-use stall, saw how much forwarding saves, and removed the stall by scheduling instructions - exactly what compilers do for in-order pipelines.
